#Virtual_Space_Roaming🔰Let's read the table so we don't become a mere shopfront🔺Maybe the development model is something other than buying Ronaldo!🔸Iran's young caravan — a nation that has been through war — in days when even coming and going through the skies was difficult for it, reached sixth place in Asia with 19 golds, 18 silvers, and 15 bronzes;◽It became the best country in West Asia by a wide margin◾It reeled in 6 more gold medals than the previous edition of the competitions◽Its girls claimed a 15-medal share of the caravan's 52 medals◾And it was only 3 more golds away from achieving the best result in its history...Hats off to them and may they stay in good health.🔸Saudi Arabia, too, reached twentieth place in the table with 3 golds, 2 silvers, and 9 bronzes — above Singapore and below Vietnam; it maintained the gap it has always had with Iran, and likely, with the rise of Iranian female athletes in recent years, that gap will only widen.🔸Of course, I have always avoided/avoid this kind of induction, but since for several years the most inefficient and backward development model — one that views every manifestation of development as a mere shopfront — has been used to humiliate Iranians, I say: Perhaps the "development model" should be something other than buying foreign players at ten times their market price for a seductive show in the domestic league... It is where the Portuguese Ronaldo cannot take the field in place of a Saudi athlete and win a medal that the true measure of nations' progress finally becomes clear... Just as in wartime, the true measure of a cheap military force — one whose software, hardware, and infantry arise from its own soil, science, and national awareness — is revealed against the world's greatest military power; and the impurity of an expensive army becomes apparent when, after being branded a "milking cow" and buying up countless fighter jets and Patriot systems and hiring hundreds of thousands of mercenaries from other countries, they are ultimately deployed to fight against a besieged land with the least possible military logistics — and get stuck in the mud.🔸Which problem does sports solve? To be honest, none! It was never supposed to solve any particular problem from the start, but it is a good mirror for reflecting a society's perception... If on the day our club team, worth about 15 million dollars, loses to a Saudi club team worth about 200 million dollars, we feel backwardness and humiliation — but when in a global event the gap between Iranian and Saudi national players reveals itself to this degree and we do not look at it "differently," it means that before anything else, we have lost the capacity for independent thinking — we too have become a shopfront!💬 Mohammad Sadegh Faramarzi🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram@Kayhan_Online

She described the charges brought in this case as "extremely serious." This alleged plot was thwarted at the same time as the Jewish High Holidays, the anniversary of last year's terrorist attack on the Heaton Park synagogue, and a rise in reports of antisemitic incidents across the UK. Exclusive: A US official says Rubio ordered the Iranian delegation to leave American soil.

According to a US official and another informed source, Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, on Monday, after negotiations reached an impasse, asked the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran at the United Nations General Assembly to leave the country immediately.

Why does this matter?
Although members of the Iranian delegation were expected to leave American soil soon, Rubio's move is seen as a harsh and unusual diplomatic reaction and, amid futile efforts to end the conflicts, lays bare the depth of mistrust between the two countries.

Qatari mediators tried to untangle the diplomatic knot between Washington and Tehran, but little progress was made, as neither side was willing to back down from its positions.

Among those ordered to leave New York was Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister and Rubio's counterpart.

Account of informed sources
This US official stated: "Marco Rubio expelled the Iranian delegation whose presence had dragged on beyond acceptable limits. The General Assembly was over and it was time for them to go."

What happened behind the scenes?
On Monday morning, the White House hoped that progress would be made in the negotiations with Tehran later in the day; however, by late afternoon it became clear that the negotiations had reached an impasse.

According to this US official, on Monday evening, the United States mission to the United Nations, on Rubio's orders, informed the Iranian mission that Araghchi's accompanying delegation must leave New York immediately.

The Iranian delegation, including Araghchi, headed to the airport a few hours later and left New York for Doha on a flight at 1:20 a.m. Tuesday.

The second source also confirmed that the US had demanded the departure of the Iranian delegation, but noted that Araghchi's travel plan to return to Tehran had already been set for Monday night.

What is the next step?
According to regional sources, Qatari mediators continue consultations with both sides over their proposed compromise plan.

Donald Trump, the US President, on Wednesday, in response to reporters' questions about how to reach an agreement with a government he calls unpredictable, said: "Maybe I'll attack them (blow them up). Maybe I'll target them; we have to make this decision. Either we attack them or we reach an agreement. But the time for this decision is near, and this situation will end very soon, in one way or another."

Regarding this edition's special focus on the second and third imposed wars and the children of Minab, he explained: Out of respect for the martyred children of Minab, all of the festival's usual special sections have been eliminated, and only the special Minab section and award will be held. A dedicated poster and statuette have been designed for this section. Additionally, in the Minab screenwriting competition, which drew widespread participation, 4 top proposals were selected from among 423 submissions and their screenplays were completed, with the winners to be announced during the festival.
🔸The secretary of the 38th Children and Adolescents Film Festival continued, noting structural changes and the addition of new sections to the event, and added: In order to recognize the efforts of the technical crew in children's cinema, who are less visible at festivals, awards have been added for technical categories such as acting, editing, and music. New sections have also been added to this edition, including artificial intelligence, to address emerging technologies; a documentary section in workshop format; and the Mirror section, aimed at reviewing and analyzing works broadcast on platforms and television, with a focus on audience engagement and product development.
🔸He added: The Adolescents Filmmaking Olympiad, which was halted last year due to special circumstances, will also be held this year alongside the festival in Isfahan.
🔸Jafari announced the names of the 15 feature-length fiction films selected for the competition section of this edition of the Children's Festival as follows: Badbadak-ha, Pelk-e Parishan-e Parvaneh, Do Tofangdar, Shootinga, Arous-e Cheshmeh, Amu-ye Bacheh-ha, Kakaluti, Kuch, Gorgi Khan, Man Jasouzan Nistam, Nabegheh va Div-e Sangi, Negahbanan-e Khorshid, Noor, Varkana, and Yeki Miad Donbalam. #Adab_va_Honar🔘 Bale | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram@Kayhan_Online

spectatorindex White House agreement on artificial intelligence

Joint commitment on accountability for frontier models

To build a hopeful future for the people of America and around the world, we believe that every company has a duty to develop its technology safely and in a way that builds trust with customers and the general public.

The starting point on this path is that all companies engaged in training and deploying frontier models must have strong internal control processes and mechanisms in place to ensure that their technology performs in line with defined objectives and that any potential flaw is immediately identified and addressed. Therefore, in addition to the usual precautionary measures, we believe that every company must implement the following four layers of oversight and auditing:

1. Implementation of rigorous internal control mechanisms to monitor the capabilities and alignment of models during the training and deployment stages, particularly in areas such as cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical threats, and to ensure that systems do not engage in intrusion or unauthorized and unintended access to technical infrastructure.

2. Delegation of authority to an internal team to ensure that all control, oversight, and detection systems operate in accordance with established standards and that identified disruptions are resolved without delay.

3. Cooperation with independent external evaluators and auditors to conduct impartial inspections of the correctness of oversight, monitoring, and error detection processes.

4. Appointment of an independent committee drawn from board members for high-level oversight, receiving periodic reports from executive teams and internal and external auditors, and ensuring the complete resolution of all reported deficiencies.

Together, these steps will provide lasting reassurance to companies, customers, and society that the technology in question performs reliably and in line with its original objectives.

Companies that are members of this agreement will meet regularly to develop standards and best practices for enhancing the safety of their systems.

Over time, codifying these mechanisms within the framework of formal laws or regulations will be a logical approach. Regardless of whether the implementation of these rules acquires a legally binding character for enterprises in the future, we consider the implementation of these controls and audits a vital necessity for guaranteeing a safe future for all, and each and every one of our organizations is committed to realizing it.

What are the consequences of fabricated polarizations for Iran?🔹Reducing the country's complex issues to binaries like "peace-seeking vs. warmongering" or "negotiation vs. war" can steer society away from a genuine conversation about national interests, costs, and foreign policy options.🔹Critics of this approach argue that negotiation should be a tool of foreign policy, not the only solution; just as defense and deterrence capabilities should not be equated with "warmongering."🔹The experience of the JCPOA and America's withdrawal from it has brought into sharper focus the debate over guaranteeing an agreement's implementation, reciprocal concessions, and preserving bargaining power. From this perspective, the core issue is not "negotiation or war," but preserving the power of choice and securing national interests.🔹False polarizations, rather than strengthening national cohesion, can deepen social divides; whereas in the face of external threats, internal cohesion, defense capability, economic strength, and active diplomacy can all serve national interests simultaneously.🔹Analysts believe that negotiation can help secure national interests when it is pursued from a position of choice, not out of compulsion and necessity. The experience of past agreements has also shown that an agreement alone, without guarantees of implementation and bargaining power, does not necessarily lead to a sustainable outcome.🔹When individuals and factions are categorized with labels like "warmonger" or "peacenik," the possibility of rational dialogue about details diminishes.🔹From the perspective of critics of polarization, a society that can discuss its differences while emphasizing shared national interests will have a greater capacity to manage foreign crises.@Farspolitics - link

IRGC: We seized the second American unmanned submarine in the Strait of Hormuz

The Naval Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed in a statement on Sunday, the fifth of Mehr, that it had identified and seized an American unmanned remotely operated underwater vehicle (UUV) in the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC statement said that its Naval Force personnel, in a "coordinated and complex operation" employing intelligence superiority and electronic warfare, trapped the subsurface vehicle, which was operating "to spy in the Strait of Hormuz."

The IRGC identified the submarine as a REMUS 600 and said it has taken it as a prize and it is now in the hands of IRGC Naval Force specialists so its data can be extracted and examined.

Media affiliated with the Islamic Republic also simultaneously released a video of the subsurface vehicle, presenting it as the "second" American UUV, or unmanned submarine, to have fallen into Iran's hands during the recent clashes in the Strait of Hormuz.

According to Iranian state media reports, this submarine is an autonomous underwater vehicle (UUV/AUV), and unlike a manned submarine, it carries no crew on board. This family of systems is used for missions including reconnaissance and countering naval mines, mapping the seabed, subsurface identification and surveillance, and gathering maritime intelligence.

Today's IRGC claim comes after, on the 17th of Shahrivar, the IRGC Naval Force had previously announced the seizure of another American subsurface vehicle near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.

CENTCOM said at the time that the submarine had stopped due to a technical malfunction and "did not contain sensitive information."

After several rounds of failed military operations and the humiliation that followed, the enemy's guard shifted to economic siege and hostility. But unfortunately, some managers, advisers, and analysts still deal with it through the negotiation guard (the catalyst of the enemy's plot).

Certainly, military threats must not be neglected or underestimated. But neither should the enemy's intensified helplessness be forgotten, nor should it be given excessive weight, breeding passivity and fear, and causing neglect of a decisive response to the economic war and siege.

Concern about the enemy's military threat and "treating negotiation as a shelter," even if it had been correct — which it was not — belonged to the stage before the enemy's repeated betrayal of negotiations and imposition of war.

When the war happened, the illusion that negotiation and agreement serve as a deterrent defense shield collapsed. Therefore, one must not again create a bubble for oneself and others and retreat into a shell of passivity; for this behavior amounts to being played by the worn-out tactic of the madman.

The economic siege (maritime and aerial), backed by military action, is a one hundred percent aggressive and criminal military action that must be answered by deploying all kinds of military and non-military threats, symmetrical and asymmetrical.

The enemy has targeted your economy; you too must forcefully strike at its economic interests and Achilles' heels in the commercial and energy domains, the infrastructure related to undersea cables, and... in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandab, the Indian Ocean, the Sea of Oman, and the Persian Gulf.

This necessary action is precisely the opposite of passive negotiation-seeking, of pressuring the military forces not to bare their claws at America's criminal partners in the region (the UAE and...), and of calming the energy market.

All polls indicate the free fall of Trump's popularity and its clear damage to the position of his political supporters in next month's congressional elections.

The pressure must not be lifted from America. In this regard, the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council has adopted intelligent and powerful positions, and it is expected that this position will not be weakened by one-sided negotiation signals.

Also, the hands of the operating forces on the ground must be opened wider, and no restrictions or constraints should be created for them.

Not the slightest notion should take shape in the enemy's mind that, in the Iranian side's view, field-oriented actions have subsided and the emphasis and reliance is only on negotiation. This notion is inherently anti-authority and even undermines bargaining power should negotiation become necessary.

When your…
entry.summary:

Source: @Kayhan_online

Deterrent Defense Shield: Negotiation or Counter-Offensive? – 1

When your opponent in a contest—a fight—changes stance, you too must change your stance and not remain passive.

America and Israel had clearly come up short in the forty-day war, and the tide had turned, prompting them to seek a ceasefire through intermediaries:

- National unity and cohesion, contrary to the plan for the January overthrow and coup, had been revived and reached its peak.
- The Strait of Hormuz had been closed, humiliating America.
- A significant portion of their offensive and defensive munitions had run out or been strategically depleted.
- Key American bases in the region had been struck. They had nearly been rendered inoperable, yet were still imposing considerable costs on the Pentagon.
- Dozens of fighter jets, helicopters, and drones had been shot down.
- Attempts to reopen the strait or penetrate deep into Iran had failed.
- Iran kept revealing new intelligence and military cards.
- Oil prices during the war had risen to $126.
- And more...

One can accept that, for certain considerations, the Iranian side agreed to a (temporary) ceasefire and would use this time to regroup and reorganize forces, capabilities, and plans.

What is not reasonable was tying the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to the ceasefire.

There was no reason that, while the hostile party had twice betrayed during negotiations and committed great and unprecedented crimes, it should receive a concession on the level of reopening the strait through that strange tweet by Mr. Araghchi.

What was America's reaction? Trump, at the same time as oil prices crashed, announced he would impose a naval blockade against Iran!

This, even though at the height of the war, under pressure from oil prices, he had been forced to suspend some oil sanctions so that Iranian oil could reach the market.

If the justification is an existential threat, Trump later raised this threat more than ten more times. And before that, he never shied away from any crime—unless he was unable to commit it.

Delving into the rest of the story regarding the "memorandum of understanding" is beyond the scope of this analysis.

Whatever judgment we hold about the memorandum of understanding—whether we call it an "honor—a great achievement" or deem it a "mirage/deception operation"—unfortunately, the stance of some of those in charge has not changed after the enemy violated the agreement.

💢To be continued

🔘 Bale | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram
@Kayhan_Online

🔰 A medal lost because of a shoe — who is accountable?! 🔸Fatemeh Mohiti-Zadeh, gold medalist at the Islamic Countries Games, came within reach of a medal at the Nagoya Asian Games — not because of any technical weakness or defeat on the field of competition, but because of an issue that apparently could easily have been prevented before the competition! 🔸After completing six heptathlon events, and with a medal within her grasp, Mohiti-Zadeh was barred from continuing and eliminated because her shoe was ruled non-compliant. Following the incident, the Athletics Federation stated in its official protest that the athlete's shoe had been approved during the equipment inspection before the competition. And if it had been approved during inspection, how did that same shoe later lead to her elimination?! 🔸At this point, it can no longer be dismissed as a simple mistake. The Athletics Federation must clarify who was responsible for checking the athlete's equipment, who reviewed the regulations governing the shoe, and why such an issue was not resolved before the competition began?! 🔸Mohiti-Zadeh did her part, but the federation's poor management cost her the medal — a management that in recent months has frittered away one opportunity after another, yet no one in the sports system has stepped up to tell it the obvious! The Ministry of Sport and Youth, as the body overseeing the performance of sports federations, has been nothing but a spectator all along, imagining that by turning a blind eye and a deaf ear, problems will resolve themselves. The case of the online gold dealer has reached the Supreme National Security Council

🔹The online gold sales platform Milli Gold, in a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, has called for an urgent order to lift restrictions on users' access to their gold held in bank vaults.

🔹The platform says restrictions imposed by the Economic Security Police and some related bodies have made it difficult to access part of its reserves and fulfill its obligations to users.

🔹In recent days, a number of Milli Gold users on social media have complained about delays in rial settlements and in receiving their physical gold. Some users have also raised concerns about the actual amount of gold backing the platform's transactions, alleging "selling empty."

🔹These concerns come as, under Central Bank regulations, online platforms must hold reserves equivalent to their obligations for gold sold, and the stored gold must be converted into standard bars with a purity of at least 995 within three months.

🔹Milli Gold, however, claims that existing governance mechanisms and bureaucracy have restricted its access to bank reserves, and that this has in turn disrupted the delivery of users' gold. The company had previously stated that users' gold is held in bank vaults.

🔸Now, given recent concerns about users' access to their gold and the claims raised about the backing of transactions, connecting all platforms to the supervisory system as quickly as possible — with online reporting of their inventory and obligations — has become more important than ever and could ease some of users' concerns.

🔗Read the full report here. @Farsna

Qom Province Appeals Court upheld, without modification, the sentence of 74 lashes for Parastoo Ahmadi and eight others from among the musicians and crew of the "Caravanserai Concert."

Lawyer Abouzar Zaman wrote on Friday on the social media platform X that, according to the ruling of Branch 16 of the Qom Appeals Court, Parastoo Ahmadi, four musicians, and four others have been sentenced to 74 lashes in addition to a two-year ban on activity in audiovisual affairs and a ban on leaving the country.

The Qom Province Criminal Court had previously convicted these nine individuals on charges of "outraging public decency through the production and publication of vulgar and immoral content on social media."

In Azar 1403, Parastoo Ahmadi published on YouTube the video of the "Caravanserai Concert," which was performed without mandatory hijab and with the accompaniment of Ehsan Birghdar, Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, and Amirali Pirnia.

After the publication of this performance, the Judiciary announced charges against those involved, and Ahmadi and two musicians accompanying her were also detained for a period.

In the preliminary ruling, the court had cited Parastoo Ahmadi's attire as well as the production, filming, and public publication of this performance on social media as among the grounds for issuing the verdict.

🔰Wandering in Cyberspace🔸A highly valuable insight into the character of the Supreme Leader of the Revolution🔸A very interesting point that became clearly evident from the first message of the new Leader of the Revolution, and is both highly valuable and rare, is that he is extremely attentive to details and also very insistent that even seemingly insignificant details be conveyed to the people with complete honesty.🔸How was the clenched fist—which has now become a symbol of resistance—first brought up?🔸In one part of the message, he said: "I had this blessing to visit his body after his martyrdom; what I saw was a mountain of steadfastness; and I heard that he had clenched the fist of his healthy hand."🔸In these same three simple sentences, interesting details have been presented. Whereas he could have easily glossed over these details and said that he saw the body of the martyred Leader and that his fist was clenched.🔸The matter of honestly declaring "I originally had a different opinion" is another clear example of this aspect of his character, which needs no further explanation.🔸In his condolence message for the passing of Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani, various such subtleties can be seen, one of which is this sentence: "This honorable scholar spent his entire noble life—except for the first few years of childhood—on the path of learning and teaching and research"🔸When it is said that a person spent his life on the path of learning and teaching, it does not mean the period of his childhood, but the Supreme Leader of the Revolution does not simply pass over this seemingly obvious matter either, and writes his words with precision and exact details, and specifies that the matter of him having spent his life on this path does not include the first few years of childhood!🔸All this precision and honesty in expression at the highest position of the country is very valuable and, God willing, heralds a much better future.Mohammadreza Nazari🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram@Kayhan_Online

🔹AI…
entry.summary:

Source: @FarsNA

False cheating accusations against students due to software errors

🔹AI detectors used to identify cheating among school and university students have come under scrutiny in new research for significant errors, in some cases mistakenly flagging completely human-written text as AI-generated.

🔹Investigations show these tools do not detect the true origin of the text; instead, they calculate the probability of AI-generated text based on statistical features and writing style.

🔹In one experiment, a completely human-written text was assessed by 5 commercial tools as anywhere from "zero percent" to "100 percent" AI-generated.

🔹These systems have also been reported to make more errors with people whose first language is not English; in a study of 91 real TOEFL essays, an average of 61 percent of human-written texts were mistakenly identified as AI-generated.

🔹Following these problems, universities such as Waterloo in Canada and Cape Town have stopped using Turnitin's AI detection score and have emphasized relying on evidence such as drafts, edit history, learning process, and conversations with the student.
